common.detail_routed: This message would be sent to: {outputs}.
common.detail_deferred: {person} is not to be disturbed right now — {entities}. The message would wait, and be delivered at {until}.
common.detail_presence: This target does not notify everybody in every situation: its presence rule is {rule}, and {person} is currently {state}.
common.detail_silenced: {person} is not to be disturbed right now — {entities}. Only a critical alert would get through.
common.detail_silenced_temporary: {person} has been left in peace for a while, until {until}. Only a critical alert would get through.
common.detail_no_outputs: No device is listed for {person}, so there is nowhere to send this.
common.detail_not_in_audience: {person} is not one of the people {target} notifies.
common.detail_unknown_person: {target} wants to notify {person}, who is not in the list of people this house notifies.
common.detail_recursion: Every device listed for {person} points back at Notify Switchboard itself, so the message would go round in circles.
common.detail_expired: A message kept back for {person} would be given up: it would have waited too long to still be worth delivering.
common.detail_not_notified: {person} heard nothing the last time {target} went off, so the back-to-normal message does not concern {person}.
common.detail_silenced_floor: {person} is not to be disturbed right now — {entities}, and only messages marked “{floor}” or above get through. A critical alert always does.
common.detail_unknown_target: “{target}” is no longer one of the messages this house knows how to send, so there is nowhere to deliver this one.
common.detail_delivery_failed: This message was handed to the devices listed for {person} and none of them took it, so it did not arrive.

user.title: Set up Notify Switchboard
user.description: Notify Switchboard decides who is told, on what, and when; your phones and your speakers are what ring — it never rings anything itself. Once it is installed, open its options: add the people of the house and their devices first, then one target per alert.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Notify Switchboard is already installed. One is all you need.

init.title: Notify Switchboard
init.description: Start with the people of the house: which devices each of them is told on, and when they are not to be disturbed. Then create one target per alert — a water leak, a gate left open — choosing who should hear about it.

menu_options.ttl: How long a message set aside stays useful
menu_options.test_target: Send a test message through a target
menu_options.edit_target_escalation: What happens when the house is empty

person.title: Add somebody
person.description: Pick who you want to add. The next screen already offers their phones and their Focus mode.

data_description.entity_id: Whether they are at home can be used to decide if they should be told.

edit_person.title: Change somebody's devices
edit_person.description: Pick who you want to edit. The next screen opens already filled in with what is saved.

person_outputs.title: Changing the devices of {person}
person_outputs.description: Which devices does {person} get notifications on, and when should they not be disturbed?

data_description.outputs: Their phones are already ticked. You can add a device that is not set up yet: it will be used as soon as it shows up.
data_description.silence_entities: A schedule, a switch, or the Focus mode of their iPhone: while it is on, their notifications wait.

person_advanced.title: Setting up the night of {person}
person_advanced.description: What time their night ends, and how to hand them in the morning what was set aside. Both answers are optional, and leaving the wake time empty is an answer: messages then wait for the not-to-be-disturbed period to end by itself, when it announces an end — a schedule does — and are given up otherwise.

data.summary: Sum it all up in one message

data_description.wake_time: The time the night ends, for example 07:00. What was set aside during the night is delivered then, instead of being lost. Empty: messages wait for the not-to-be-disturbed period to end, when it announces an end.
data_description.summary: One notification on waking, listing everything that was set aside, instead of one notification per message. On by default.

edit_person_advanced.title: Setting up somebody's night
edit_person_advanced.description: Pick whose night you want to set up. Their devices and their not-to-be-disturbed periods are left exactly as they are.

data_description.entity_id: This person will no longer be told by any target. Confirm to remove them.

target.title: A target: one alert, and who hears about it
target.description: A target is one alert of the house — a water leak, a gate left open — and the people to tell when it goes off. These five answers are enough: importance, presence, buttons and wording all have a sensible value already and are set up later.

data_description.slug: Lowercase letters, no spaces, for example water_leak. This name works behind the scenes; once created, it does not change. It becomes notify.switchboard_water_leak.
data_description.name: The name people see. It is also the text sent when the alert supplies none.
data_description.alert_entity: The Home Assistant alert this target goes with. Needed for the Acknowledge button.
data_description.audience: The people concerned, and a speaker or a tablet if you want one. Nobody else hears anything.
data_description.observer_mode: Notify Switchboard watches the alert itself. There is nothing else for you to do: the moment the alert goes off, people are told. This is the recommended way.

target_saved.title: Target saved
target_saved.description:
One thing is left to do, once and for all: copy this block into your configuration, replace binary_sensor.CHANGE_ME with the sensor to watch, then restart Home Assistant.

```yaml
{snippet}
```

The block follows the choice you have just made: if Notify Switchboard watches the alert directly, there is nobody to declare here; if not, this is exactly what connects the alert to Notify Switchboard.

Everything else — importance, presence, buttons, wording — already has a sensible value. Tick the box below to set them up right away, or come back later through “Advanced settings of a target” in this menu.

data_description.advanced: Leave it unticked to save this target as it is. Ticked, it is saved when the next screen is submitted.

target_advanced.title: Advanced settings of {target}
target_advanced.description: Everything about {target} that already has a sensible value. Nothing here is required, and what you leave alone keeps the value it has.

data.default_data: Technical settings added to every message

data_description.default_priority: Only a critical alert gets through when somebody is not to be disturbed or has put the target on hold.
data_description.presence_rule: Does somebody have to be at home, to be out, or does it not matter, to be told?
data_description.allow_acknowledge: Adds a button to the notification that turns the alert off.
data_description.snooze_minutes: Durations in minutes, comma separated, for example 15, 60. Empty: no "later" button at all.
data_description.default_data: If the message already says the same thing, the message wins.
data_description.message: Optional, and used only when Notify Switchboard watches the alert itself. Empty: the name of the target is sent. Advanced users can write a template.
data_description.done_message: Optional, sent when the alert turns off, if Notify Switchboard watches it itself. Empty: a ready-made text is sent.
data_description.default_title: Title used when the call gives none, and for every message Notify Switchboard sends on its own.
data_description.clear_done: Take the back-to-normal notification off the phones that received it, once the alert is over. Off by default: it rings, then it stays.

edit_target.title: Edit a target
edit_target.description: Pick the target to edit. The next screen opens already filled in with what is saved.

edit_target_advanced.title: Advanced settings of a target
edit_target_advanced.description: Pick the target whose advanced settings you want to open. Its alert and the people it tells are left exactly as they are.

data_description.slug: Whatever used it to reach people will no longer reach anybody. Confirm to delete this target.

data.critical_payload: Make phones ring for critical alerts

data_description.default_target: Used when nothing else is said.
data_description.critical_payload: A critical alert then rings the phone even when it is set to Do Not Disturb. On by default; it only concerns the Home Assistant app.

ttl.title: How long a message set aside stays useful
ttl.description: A message set aside while somebody was not to be disturbed is not necessarily worth delivering twelve hours later. Say, per importance, how long it is still worth delivering. An empty field means it never expires. Critical alerts are never set aside, so they have no delay here.

data_description.info: In minutes, counted from the moment the message was set aside.
data_description.normal: In minutes, counted from the moment the message was set aside.
data_description.high: In minutes, counted from the moment the message was set aside. Empty by default: these messages never expire.

test_target.title: Send a test message through a target
test_target.description: Sends one real test message, to everybody this target tells.

data_description.slug: The target to try. The message counts like any other.

test_person.title: Send somebody a test message
test_person.description: Sends one real test message to this person, through a target that tells them.

data_description.entity_id: The target used by default is used when it tells this person, otherwise the first target that tells them.

test_result.title: Test result

target_escalation.title: What happens when the house is empty
target_escalation.description: What {target} does when nobody it tells is at home. Nothing else about it is touched. This choice only matters when the target also tells people who are out: if it only tells people who are in, an empty house means nobody is told at all, and there is nothing left to raise.

data.escalate_when_nobody_home: Raise the importance when the house is empty

data_description.escalate_when_nobody_home: One step louder, for that message only: not very important becomes normal, normal becomes important, important becomes critical. An alert that is already critical does not move, and presence still decides who is told.

edit_target_escalation.title: What happens when the house is empty
edit_target_escalation.description: Pick the target to set up. Everything else about it is left alone.

error.not_a_person: Pick somebody from the people of the house.
error.recursive_output: A device cannot point back at Notify Switchboard itself.
error.component_service_output: This is not a device: pick a phone, a speaker or a tablet.
error.invalid_output: This name holds characters that are not allowed.
error.invalid_entity: This does not exist (any more) in your home.
error.invalid_slug: Lowercase letters, digits and the _ sign only.
error.duplicate_slug: Another target already goes by this name.
error.invalid_priority: Pick one of: not very important, normal, important, critical.
error.invalid_presence_rule: Pick one of: always, only people at home, only people who are out.
error.unknown_person: This target wants to tell somebody who is not in the list of people this house notifies.
error.invalid_snooze_minutes: Use whole, positive minutes, comma separated.
error.invalid_default_data: This field is for technical settings; leave it empty if you are not sure.

abort.nothing_to_remove: There is nothing to remove yet.
abort.nothing_to_edit: There is nothing to edit yet.
abort.nothing_to_test: No target tells this person anything, so there is nothing to send them. Add them to a target first.

unknown_target.title: A target that was asked for does not exist
unknown_target.description: Something asked for the target “{slug}”, which does not exist. The message was given up. Create that target, or fix whatever asks for it.

missing_output.title: A device no longer answers
missing_output.description: The device “{output}” has received nothing several times in succession: it does not exist, or every send ended in an error. The messages meant for it are lost. Repair it, or take it out of the person's devices.

invalid_service_target.title: Something keeps asking for a target that does not exist
invalid_service_target.description: Notify Switchboard cannot find the target “{value}”. Something — most often a card or a script left on a renamed target — keeps asking for it. Fix it, or create that target.

invalid_service_person.title: Something keeps naming somebody it cannot tell
invalid_service_person.description: Notify Switchboard cannot find “{value}”: that person is not in the list of people of the house, or is not told by this target. Fix whatever asks for them, or add that person.

invalid_service_calls_many.title: Something keeps asking with names that do not exist
invalid_service_calls_many.description: Notify Switchboard has now refused more than {count} different targets or people. Rather than one warning per name, this one stands for them all. Something is making up names that do not exist — most often an automation producing a wrong name. Fix it; this warning goes away when you restart Notify Switchboard.

person_without_user_id.title: Somebody is not linked to a Home Assistant account
person_without_user_id.description: {person} gets notifications with the Acknowledge and Later buttons, but their card is not linked to any Home Assistant account. Notify Switchboard therefore cannot tell who pressed, and applies the action to everybody the target tells. Link this person to their account in Settings > People, then reload Notify Switchboard.

person_without_outputs.title: Somebody has no device at all
person_without_outputs.description: At least one target tells {person}, but no device is listed for {person}: every message meant for them is lost. Open the Notify Switchboard options, edit that person and give them at least one device.

alert_entity_missing.title: A target watches an alert that does not exist
alert_entity_missing.description: The target “{slug}” watches an alert that no longer exists ({entity_id}). So it watches nothing, and its Acknowledge button turns nothing off. Create that alert, or take it out of the target's “Alert watched” field, then reload Notify Switchboard.

acknowledge_not_allowed.message: The target {target} has no Acknowledge button: it watches no alert, or the button is turned off for it.

snooze_minutes_not_offered.message: The target {target} does not offer a {minutes} min hold. It offers: {offered}.

unknown_person.message: {person} is not in the list of people Notify Switchboard knows about.

person_not_in_audience.message: {person} is not one of the people the target {target} tells.

invalid_silence_minutes.message: Peace and quiet lasts between {min} and {max} minutes; {minutes} is neither.

no_loaded_entry.message: Notify Switchboard is switched off, so it can do nothing. Switch it back on, then try again.

options.critical: Critical — gets through even when somebody is not to be disturbed

options.home_only: Only people who are at home

acknowledge.name: Acknowledge
acknowledge.description: Turns off the alert a target watches, exactly as the Acknowledge button of a notification does.

target.name: Target
target.description: The target concerned (its short identifier). It must watch an alert and offer the Acknowledge button.

snooze.name: Put on hold
snooze.description: Stops the messages of one target for a while, for one person or for everybody that target tells.

target.name: Target
target.description: The target concerned (its short identifier), the one to put on hold.

minutes.name: Minutes
minutes.description: For how long. It has to be one of the durations the target offers.

person.name: Person
person.description: For whom. Leave empty for everybody that target tells.

unsnooze.name: Take off hold
unsnooze.description: Starts the messages again straight away, without waiting for the hold to run out.

target.name: Target
target.description: The target concerned (its short identifier), the one to start again.

person.name: Person
person.description: For whom. Leave empty for everybody that target tells.

silence.name: Do not disturb somebody
silence.description: Stops disturbing somebody for a while, for every target. Their own schedules and switches are left untouched; only a critical alert still gets through.

person.name: Person
person.description: Who is not to be disturbed. They have to be in the list of people this house notifies.

minutes.name: Minutes
minutes.description: For how long: from 1 minute to 1440 (a day).

unsilence.name: Make somebody reachable again
unsilence.description: Cancels straight away a do-not-disturb set by the action above. Does nothing when the person was not left in peace that way.

explain.name: Explain
explain.description: Answers the question “what would happen to a message sent right now to this target?”, person by person, without sending anything. Call it asking for the answer.

target.name: Target
target.description: The target concerned (its short identifier), the one to look at.

priority.name: Importance
priority.description: The importance to assume. Leave empty for the one the target uses by default, exactly as a real message does.

person.name: Person
person.description: Whom to answer about. Leave empty for everybody that target tells.
